scope: P13/G13 bounded Windows filesystem, search, Git, PowerShell, PDF, workspace-authority services, retained G06 regressions, and the owner-approved fresh-build recovery qualification
acceptance: Filesystem/search/Git/shell/PDF behavior and security tests pass.

toolchain.json: nlohmann-json 3.12.0#2 via the pinned vcpkg manifest

recovery_qualification.diagnosis: The same-process diagnostics rotation fixture used arbitrary SuspendThread/ResumeThread synchronization and could suspend its writer while holding a process-local lock. The failed command proves the isolated G06 registration failure; the internal deadlock attribution is a source-analysis inference corroborated by the two live process snapshots documented in P13-006.
recovery_qualification.repair_characterization: The repair replaces arbitrary thread suspension with private injected cooperative checkpoints, adds per-test progress output, and adds a 120-second CTest fail-safe. It does not serialize the suite or alter P13 native-tool production behavior.
recovery_guardrails: The baseline commit, direct repair commit and tree, failed record identity and SHA-256, both failed-output hashes, exact command, working directory, role, and parallelism are pinned in the runner.
The runner rejects changed tracked, staged, unstaged, or untracked build inputs, permits only the active recorder streams, and rejects any second successful reuse of this failed record.

Every affected retained G06/G13 target is incrementally rebuilt before the unchanged parallel G06|G13 selection, inventory, artifact, Forsetti, ledger, no-Python, no-attribution, and repository-integrity checks.
recovery_qualification.conclusion: The owner-authorized recovery preserves the successful fresh affected-target build, rebuilds every input affected by the deterministic diagnostics repair, and supplies a complete passing test and post-build evidence pass. It is sufficient for this machine-scoped alpha G13 gate.

independent_checks: All three named Git commits and trees exist. The repair is the direct child of the fresh-build baseline, the recovery-control commit is the direct child of the repair, and current HEAD plus origin/main resolved to the recovery-control commit at review start.

The failed command record and both output files were independently re-hashed. Their hashes match the record; the stdout reaches the test marker only after the fresh affected-target build and isolates the result to one failed Infrastructure.UnitTests registration after eleven passes.

The recovery command record and both output files were independently re-hashed. It ran from D:\GitHub\Forge-Conductor-Windows-Edition, exited 0 without timeout, retained empty stderr, and its stdout reports all twelve selected CTest registrations passing in 12.19 seconds.
The recovery stdout reports exactly 1007 G13 assertions, four retained G06 registrations, eight G13 registrations, retained G12 static validation, and eighteen artifact hashes.

The recovery runner pins the exact baseline, repair commit/tree, failed record and outputs, command identity, working directory, role, and parallelism; it rejects unrelated inputs and prior successful reuse before rebuilding all affected targets.

Source inspection confirms the repair removes every SuspendThread/ResumeThread call from the retained diagnostics suite, uses bounded cooperative checkpoints after stage creation and before publication validation, keeps those seams private to injected test access, and leaves normal production construction without an observer.

All eighteen retained Debug artifacts were independently re-hashed and match the hashes printed by the recovery command. Each of the fifteen executable artifacts independently reports PE machine 0x8664 (AMD64).

The sealed Forsetti tree was independently recomputed with the runner's ordinal-path algorithm as 171 files, 723455 bytes, and SHA-256 cfc377fee173cddc515f18f9c28db58e10b468402a72541a1f0ad524a1073c28.
The successful runner reached repository diff, ledger, no-Python, and no-attribution checks after testing and artifact hashing. Its exit 0 proves those checks passed at the recovery boundary.
This Validator performed no build, test execution, validation-runner invocation, ledger update, gate-result update, or production-code mutation.
limitations: This approval is scoped to P13/G13 native services on the current owner machine in x64 Debug. It does not qualify Release, ARM64, another machine, or a clean environment.
The seventeen P13 MCP parity rows remain open. P14 owns registered schemas, routing, aliases, defaults, metadata, and wire-response evidence.

Dedicated post-alpha security hardening, broad installer qualification, clean-environment reproduction, and bespoke UI polish remain deferred under OWNER-002. Planned UI automation remains in scope for its later gate.

The failed recorder output proves a single isolated Infrastructure.UnitTests failure after a completed build, but not the internal deadlock cause. That cause is an evidence-backed source-analysis inference documented in P13-006; the deterministic repair and complete recovery pass are the functional confirmation.
CTest's mutable LastTest.log for the recovery contains only invocation start/end markers. Detailed per-registration results are retained in the recovery command's SHA-256-pinned stdout instead.
Passing G13 is not a claim that the MCP server, Manager, GUI, installer, or owner-qualified internal alpha is complete.
